bus.plain: A junction point in a power grid where power lines, generators, and towns connect.
bus.technical: A node in an electrical power system where transmission lines, generators, and loads interconnect at a common voltage level.

pu.plain: A percentage-like scale where 1.0 means exactly normal or nominal operating level.
pu.technical: Per-unit system expressing electrical quantities as fractions of defined base values (e.g. 1.0 p.u. = nominal voltage).

voltage.plain: The electrical pressure pushing electric current through the power grid.
voltage.technical: Electric potential difference between two points, maintained within nominal limits (typically 0.95 to 1.05 p.u.).

frequency.plain: The heartbeat of the electrical grid (typically 60 Hz or 50 Hz), showing whether generation matches consumption.
frequency.technical: Rotational frequency of synchronized generators across the grid, governed by the swing equation balancing mechanical power and electrical demand.

generator.plain: A power plant that produces electrical energy to power the grid.
generator.technical: Synchronous machine converting mechanical torque into active and reactive electrical power, controlled by governor and AVR systems.

synchronous_condenser.plain: A rotating machine that provides voltage stability without burning fuel.
synchronous_condenser.technical: Unloaded synchronous motor operating to supply or absorb reactive power for voltage regulation and system inertia.

transmission_line.plain: High-voltage wires that carry electricity over long distances between junctions.
transmission_line.technical: Conductors modeled with series impedance and shunt admittance carrying power between grid substations.

transformer.plain: Equipment that steps voltage up for long-distance transport or down for safe local use.
transformer.technical: Electromagnetic device transferring AC energy between different voltage circuits through mutual induction.

breaker.plain: An automated switch that opens to isolate faulty equipment or lines.
breaker.technical: Circuit breaker designed to interrupt fault currents under protection relay commands.

state_estimation.plain: The mathematical process that calculates the most likely true grid condition from noisy sensor readings.
state_estimation.technical: Weighted Least Squares (WLS) algorithm minimizing measurement residuals to estimate complex voltage states [V, theta].

residual.plain: The difference between what a sensor reports and what physics says it should be.
residual.technical: Difference vector r = z - h(x) between observed telemetry z and estimated measurement function h(x).

normalized_residual.plain: The measurement difference divided by expected sensor noise to detect outliers.
normalized_residual.technical: Residual r_i divided by the square root of diagonal element of residual covariance matrix Omega = R - H(H^T R^-1 H)^-1 H^T.

chi_square.plain: A statistical test to check if overall sensor errors are within normal random noise limits.
chi_square.technical: Global detection criterion J(x) = sum((z_i - h_i(x))^2 / sigma_i^2) evaluated against Chi-Square threshold with m-n degrees of freedom.

false_data_injection.plain: A cyberattack where sensor readings are secretly modified to trick operators or automated controls.
false_data_injection.technical: Cyberattack injecting malicious vector 'a' into telemetry z_bad = z + a, crafted to bypass or trigger bad data detection.

replay.plain: A cyberattack that repeats recorded past sensor data to hide ongoing physical disturbances.
replay.technical: Cyber event re-transmitting valid historical telemetry frames to mask contemporary state deviations.

denial_of_service.plain: An attack that cuts off communication lines so the control room loses visibility.
denial_of_service.technical: Disruption of SCADA communication channels causing packet loss, timeout, or frozen state observations.

malicious_command.plain: An unauthorized instruction sent to field equipment to force unsafe operating setpoints.
malicious_command.technical: Tampering with supervisory control signals (e.g. generator setpoint, capacitor switching) to induce instability.

telemetry.plain: Data measurements (voltage, power, current) sent from sensors to the control room.
telemetry.technical: Digital sensor measurement stream sampled at discrete time intervals and transmitted via industrial protocols.

observed_value.plain: The raw number received by the control room from a sensor (which could contain noise or tampering).
observed_value.technical: Telemetry value received by the EMS, tagged with OBSERVED provenance.

estimated_value.plain: The value calculated by the physics mathematical model after filtering sensor noise.
estimated_value.technical: Optimal state calculation h(x_hat) derived from weighted least squares state estimation.

ground_truth.plain: The real physical condition of the simulated grid, kept completely secret from detection algorithms.
ground_truth.technical: True state vector computed directly by the power flow solver, firewalled from detector and analyst modules.

digital_twin.plain: A realistic software simulation of an electrical grid used for testing, research, and learning.
digital_twin.technical: High-fidelity virtual model replicating electrical and supervisory dynamics in-process for study without physical risk.

scada.plain: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition: the central computer system used to monitor and manage the grid.
scada.technical: Industrial control system architecture comprising RTUs, PLCs, communications, and master stations for grid operations.

avr.plain: An automated controller on a generator that adjusts output to keep nearby voltage steady.
avr.technical: Closed-loop feedback controller on synchronous generators adjusting field excitation current to maintain terminal voltage setpoint.

coi.plain: A combined measurement of overall generator speeds to calculate the grid's average frequency.
coi.technical: Inertia-weighted aggregate frequency model representing rotational kinetic energy dynamics across all interconnected generators.

mitigation.plain: Corrective control action taken to stop an ongoing problem and return the grid to safety.
mitigation.technical: Pre-approved, allowlisted operational interventions (sensor quarantine, setpoint reset, line re-routing) to restore nominal operation.

verification.plain: A 3-way test comparing before the attack, during the problem, and after the fix to prove the remedy worked.
verification.technical: Comparative simulation evaluating Baseline, Unmitigated, and Mitigated physical trajectories to calculate objective improvement.
